reason: Source lines are real (service.py:215, sandbox.py:189/221/223-224/690/692 all match). The fingerprint is unique among findings.json records and the sink and validation-plan check out. Two wording problems are material. (1) Root-cause attribution is too narrow. Line 221 spares any new baseline-session process that is windowed, or whose non-baseline ancestor is windowed. That holds with fully truthful window pids: a newly opened windowed app such as Thunar, mousepad or xfce4-terminal, and any helper or script it spawns in the Xfce session's sid, is spared by design (docstring at line 189). _NET_WM_PID forgery is only one extra way to get there, and the image has no python, xprop or compiler (Dockerfile:17-21), so a forged pid would need a hand-written X client. The record's claimed_root_cause now covers both: the exemption is keyed on window presence and a client-declared pid, not on a control-plane-verifiable link. (2) The second blocker is partly answerable from source: _close_gui_burst pops the burst (service.py:233), kills (235), takes one manifest (236-240) and then never watches again, so a survivor's later writes are unmonitored. Only whether a process actually survives in the real image is open. Also, images/desktop/agentbox-desktop-start:30 launches startxfce4 in the start script's session, so Xfce-launched apps inherit a burst-start sid and are not killed at line 218. Terminal shells almost certainly get a new sid, but that is not observable from source. I kept the fingerprint (same sink and line 221) and kept the verdict at needs_validation: the live process, session and window layout needs the running image, which this sandbox cannot provide. No sandboxed run was needed and no artifacts were produced.

record.title: gui_strays exempts burst-launched uid-1001 processes from the stray kill based on window ownership, including the client-declared _NET_WM_PID
record.description: At GUI-burst close, AgentBox._stop_gui_strays collects uid-1001 processes and the set of window-owning pids and calls gui_strays. A new (non-baseline, non-exec-rooted) uid-1001 process that lives in a session that existed at burst start (base_sids) is spared whenever it is 'windowed': its own pid is in window_pids, or a NON-baseline ancestor's pid is in window_pids. window_pids come from `xdotool getwindowpid`, which returns the _NET_WM_PID property each X client sets for itself. Two routes can therefore spare background work started during the burst. (a) Without any forgery, a newly opened windowed app in the burst-start session (for example a file manager or editor started during the burst) exempts the scripts and children it spawns, because the ancestor clause only requires the windowed ancestor to be non-baseline. (b) A GUI client that declares another process's pid in _NET_WM_PID makes that process, even a headless one, look windowed. Either way the process can survive the close and keep modifying /workspace outside any monitored burst, which weakens the N-1 partial mitigation. Children of a PRE-EXISTING windowed baseline app are still killed, because the ancestor clause excludes baseline ancestors. Processes in a new session (terminal shells, setsid or nohup) are killed regardless of window (line 218). In the image, Xfce is started by the start script (agentbox-desktop-start:30), so apps launched from Xfce probably inherit a burst-start sid. This is not observable from source. The image has no python, xprop or compiler (Dockerfile:17-21), so route (b) needs a hand-written X client.
record.claimed_root_cause: Whether a new baseline-session process is spared is decided by window presence, derived from X window properties (including the client-settable _NET_WM_PID via xdotool getwindowpid) and a 'new windowed ancestor' heuristic, rather than by a control-plane-verifiable link such as the docker-exec ancestry already tracked. Target-controlled GUI clients, or any legitimately windowed app launched during the burst, therefore decide which of their descendants are treated as windowed apps or helpers and escape the kill.

trace.description: Burst close ingests attacker-influenced container output: calls desktop_processes(sid) to get the process list and window pids, then gui_strays to classify which new uid-1001 processes to kill.
Window pids come from `xdotool search --onlyvisible --name .` then `xdotool getwindowpid $w`, i.e. the client-set _NET_WM_PID property, parsed into the wins set at line 692.

A new baseline-session process is marked windowed (p.pid in window_pids, or a non-baseline ancestor pid in window_pids) and consequently NOT appended to the kill list at lines 223-224, so it survives the burst close.

evidence.description: wins = {int(x) ...} parsed from container-side xdotool getwindowpid output; the exemption input is controlled by the GUI clients inside the sandbox.

windowed = p.pid in window_pids or any(a.pid in window_pids and a.pid not in baseline for a in ancestors(p)); windowed -> not killed. The ancestor clause spares helpers of any newly created windowed app even with truthful window pids.

Docstring states windowed apps and their helpers (and burst-start processes and docker-exec-launched tools) are intentionally left running, so the only gate for a baseline-session process is window ownership.
startxfce4 is launched from the container start script, so Xfce-launched apps likely share a burst-start session id (base_sids) and are not caught by the new-session kill at sandbox.py:218.
_close_gui_burst pops the burst (233), runs the stray kill (235) and takes a single final manifest (236-240); nothing monitors /workspace afterwards, so any survivor's later writes are unrecorded.

blockers: Reachability in agentbox-desktop:0.1: whether, using only GUI input (click/type/key), a prompt-injected agent can get a uid-1001 process into a session that existed at burst start (base_sids) that either owns a visible window reported by `xdotool getwindowpid`, or descends from a newly created windowed process (for example a script run from a file manager or app window opened during the burst), or has its pid forged into another client's _NET_WM_PID. Real session ids (whether launcher, terminal or file-manager spawned processes inherit the Xfce start-script sid or get a new setsid session, which line 218 kills regardless) and real _NET_WM_PID values are not observable from source or from a pure-function harness over gui_strays, and the Docker daemon is unavailable offline. The pure-function harness already confirms the exemption logic itself.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable, network-less agentbox-desktop:0.1 sandbox: open a GUI burst with a GUI tool call. Using GUI input only, (a) open a file manager or editor window during the burst and from it run a script that appends a timestamp to a dummy file /workspace/_v15_probe every ~2s; and (b) separately, with a hand-written X client, set _NET_WM_PID of a window to the pid of a headless background writer started from a burst-start-session launcher. Just before close, record `ps -eo pid=,ppid=,sid=,uid=,args=` and `for w in $(xdotool search --onlyvisible --name .); do xdotool getwindowpid $w; done` to capture the real session ids and window-pid set, and feed them through the real gui_strays to predict survivors. Let the burst close on idle; then read the gui_processes_stopped audit entry and check whether /workspace/_v15_probe's mtime keeps advancing after close. Non-destructive: touches only the dummy probe file; kill the probe and discard the sandbox afterward.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner reproduces the same probe on the live deployed image and config to confirm the image's session-id and _NET_WM_PID semantics and that a spared process (or its child) modifies /workspace after burst close; collect the gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes audit entries and the manifest diff as evidence. Fix check: exempt only burst-start (baseline) processes and control-plane docker-exec-launched components, deriving ownership from a control-plane-verifiable link (for example the exec/ancestry already tracked) rather than window presence or the client-declared _NET_WM_PID. Non-destructive: dummy file only.
